forecasts.name: Efficient-Market Skeptic · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: The recent rapid ascent to $247 invites profit taking and demand destruction. A partial mean-reverting pullback toward $222 is underpriced by headline-fixated bulls.

forecasts.name: Adaptation Optimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Ample Black Sea flows and farmer supply responses across key origins are actively deflating wheat prices toward lower ranges.

forecasts.name: Scott Irwin (farmdoc) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Futures efficiently reflect current fundamentals. A drop below $222 within two months is possible under harvest pressure, but markets are broadly priced in.

forecasts.name: Crowd Follower · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Consensus sits at 28%. Recent spot wheat price gains make a sharp drop into December slightly less probable, so I nudge down just a touch.

forecasts.name: European Commission DG AGRI (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: While export competition from Russia is fierce, tight timeline and input cost floors limit a rapid plunge below $222/mt by December.

forecasts.name: USDA WASDE (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: A rapid fall of over $25/mt in two months contradicts the gradual revision pace of fundamental balance sheets without a major unexpected supply arrival.

forecasts.name: IMF (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Tightening logistics from Black Sea tensions and elevated global input costs make a sharp winter collapse below $222/mt unlikely.

forecasts.name: Copa-Cogeca (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: High production costs, logistics disruptions in the Black Sea, and persistent climate stress prevent a sharp price collapse for European growers by year-end.

forecasts.name: FAO (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: A drop below $222/mt by December is unlikely given elevated Black Sea shipping risks and firm energy input costs supporting floor prices.

forecasts.name: BirdLife Europe, EEB, WWF and Greenpeace (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: With ongoing climate disruptions and Black Sea conflict risks, a sharp near-term collapse in wheat prices is unlikely as ecological stresses tighten balances.

forecasts.name: Macro / Dollar · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: The sustained macro rally across wheat and feed grains makes a sharp multi-month collapse below $222 improbable absent sudden dollar strength.

forecasts.name: Agronomist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Post-harvest pressure has already peaked in September. November and December typically stabilize as commercial buying absorbs the new crop, making a drop below $222 unlikely.

forecasts.name: IFPRI (Joseph Glauber) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Escalating Black Sea maritime conflict and freight insurance spikes make a sharp drop below $222/mt in French milling wheat unlikely over the next two months.

forecasts.name: Geopolitics Hawk · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: With Black Sea shipping entering dangerous escalation and geopolitical risk premiums mounting, a sharp collapse below $222 by December is heavily constrained.

forecasts.name: Land-Grab Realist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Wheat is on an upward trajectory amid Black Sea shipping strikes. A plunge below $222 in two months ignores sovereign offtake locking up available spot supply.

forecasts.name: Climate Pessimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: With global grain belts stressed by intense heat and prices trending up, a sudden collapse below $222 in two months is pure market complacency.
